## San Francisco Monastery on a Lima city tour

A good way to explore colonial [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) is to begin in its historic center. San Francisco Monastery complements [Plaza Mayor](/peru/place/plaza-mayor-lima/) and [Lima Cathedral](/peru/place/lima-cathedral/), offering a different perspective on the city's religious and artistic life.

## How we include the complex in a journey

On our [Lima, San Isidro and Miraflores sightseeing excursion](/peru/lima/san-francisco-san-isidro-miraflores/), San Francisco belongs to the colonial section of the route. After the historic center, we continue to [San Isidro](/peru/place/san-isidro-lima/) and [Miraflores](/peru/place/miraflores-lima/) before returning to the hotel.

This sequence is also included in our [15-day Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/). You arrive in Lima from Cusco the previous day; the sightseeing excursion takes place on the morning of the final day, after breakfast. The transfer for your international departure follows your return to the hotel.

## Catacombs and interior spaces

San Francisco is known for its catacombs, library and monastic halls. For visitors, these are distinct parts of a large complex, each with its own access arrangements. The monastery is named in the 15-day itinerary, but entry to the catacombs or particular interior rooms needs to be agreed separately before booking.

If the catacombs are your main reason for visiting, tell us when choosing your program. We will clarify what can be visited, the time required and whether it fits with your international flight. We check current opening hours and separate museum admission costs for your chosen date.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this monastery in Cusco?

No. This is San Francisco Monastery in the historic center of Lima. On our itinerary, it is a stop on the capital's sightseeing tour.

### Are the catacombs automatically included?

No. We agree on whether they can be visited within the chosen excursion. Mentioning the monastery alone does not confirm access to them.

### Can I combine the tour with a flight on the final day?

The 15-day tour includes sightseeing in Lima, a return to the hotel and then the airport transfer. We plan the flight time around that full sequence.

## San Isidro: Lima's green and residential neighborhoods

After colonial [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), San Isidro reveals a different side of the city. Its residential streets, business district and El Olivar olive grove are all of interest. This neighborhood is in Peru; it shares only its name with San Isidro in Argentina.

## What the sightseeing route includes

We introduce the district on our [Lima, San Francisco, San Isidro and Miraflores excursion](/peru/lima/san-francisco-san-isidro-miraflores/). The route first takes in [Plaza Mayor](/peru/place/plaza-mayor-lima/), the [cathedral](/peru/place/lima-cathedral/) and [San Francisco Monastery](/peru/place/san-francisco-monastery-lima/). You then see San Isidro with its olive grove, Country Club and golf course before continuing to [Miraflores](/peru/place/miraflores-lima/).

This sightseeing program is included on the final day of our [15-day four-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/). You arrive in Lima from Cusco the previous day. After the morning excursion, you return to your hotel and later transfer to the airport for an international flight.

## Olive grove and archaeological heritage

El Olivar is a historic green space in the district. To explore San Isidro more deeply, we can separately discuss a visit to [Huaca Huallamarca](/peru/place/huaca-huallamarca/), an archaeological complex among modern buildings. Its pyramid appears on this page's cover image, but entry to the site is not promised in the 15-day tour.

If you particularly want a walk through the olive grove or a museum visit, we can clarify the stops and timing in advance. Seeing the golf course on a sightseeing tour does not mean playing golf, and passing the Country Club does not include the club's services.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is San Isidro a separate city on the itinerary?

No. It is a district of Lima, visited as part of the capital's sightseeing excursion.

### Is there a separate overnight stay here?

The 15-day itinerary specifies one night in Lima at Casa Andina Premium Miraflores. Sightseeing in San Isidro does not change the accommodation to a hotel in this district.

### Do I need to purchase a sports activity separately?

The district tour introduces its urban spaces. Golf and Country Club services can be arranged separately if requested.

## Santo Domingo Monastery in Lima: courtyards, shrines and city history

**Santo Domingo Monastery and Basilica stand in the historic center of [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).** This architectural ensemble is worth visiting for more than its facade and tower: the courtyards have colonnades and old ceramic tiles, while the museum spaces reveal the life of the Dominican order and the culture of colonial Peru.

Santo Domingo in the Peruvian capital must be distinguished from the church of the same name in [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), built in a different historical setting beside the Inca temple of Coricancha. These are separate attractions in different cities.

## From Lima's foundation to the monastery complex

The Dominicans established themselves in Lima during the 16th century, shortly after the city was founded by the Spanish. The beginnings of the complex are associated with **1535**. Its buildings expanded over the following decades, and earthquakes repeatedly made the rebuilding of church spaces necessary.

Santo Domingo shows the considerable influence religious orders had in the colonial capital. Monasteries were places of worship and education and centers for preserving books and producing art. The early history of **San Marcos University, founded in 1551**, also began here.

The monastery stands within Lima's UNESCO-listed historic center. Other landmarks of this ensemble include Plaza Mayor and [Lima Cathedral](/peru/place/lima-cathedral/). Together, they make it possible to trace the city's history through nearby architectural complexes.

## What to see at Santo Domingo

The **monastery courtyards** often make the strongest impression: two-level arcades enclose greenery and a tranquil space that contrasts sharply with the busy streets outside. Historic rooms retain decorative details reflecting the complex's long development.

According to Peru's official tourism inventory, the monastery ensemble includes:

- **Historic ceramic tiles.** One of the courtyards preserves Seville-made tiles from the early 17th century.
- **Paintings and carved wood.** Religious pictures, altars and traditional wooden ceilings decorate the interiors.
- **Historic rooms and library.** These illustrate the monastery's educational role and the development of written culture in Lima.
- **Basilica and shrines.** The complex is associated with veneration of prominent Peruvian Catholic saints.

The church, courtyards, museum and other rooms may have different access arrangements. If you want a complete visit, check the rules applicable to your date, particularly if religious services or restoration work are taking place.

## Rose of Lima, Martin de Porres and Saint John Macias

Santo Domingo is closely associated with **Rose of Lima**, **Martin de Porres** and **Saint John Macias**. Their remains and relics are kept within the complex. For believers, it is a pilgrimage destination; for history enthusiasts, a monument to Peru's religious life.

Alongside its architecture and artistic decoration, these associations help explain the monastery's place in Peru's cultural memory. A normal sightseeing visit also covers several different subjects: the order's history, urban development, art and religious traditions.

## Combining the monastery with the cathedral and Casa Aliaga

From Santo Domingo, it is easy to continue walking through the historic center. [Lima Cathedral](/peru/place/lima-cathedral/) demonstrates the role of the main cathedral and its museum collections, while [Casa Aliaga](/peru/place/casa-aliaga-lima/) turns attention to the domestic architecture of the colonial capital.

We combine these three attractions in our [five-hour Lima sightseeing excursion](/peru/lima/lima-cathedral-santo-domingo-casa-aliaga-five-hours/). Together they form a cultural sequence within one city route. On the longer [33-day journey through Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/), exploring Lima's historic center is the opening stage of an extended South American itinerary.

For a detailed visit to the monastery, set aside time for its courtyards, accessible museum rooms and walks through the neighboring streets. Do not assume that naming the monument on a sightseeing itinerary automatically grants access to every part of the complex.

## Practical advice before visiting

Santo Domingo is on the walking route through Lima's old center. Wear comfortable shoes and allow time to take in the streets and courtyards. In an active church, follow dress and behavior rules; photography may be restricted in certain rooms.

Restoration work has taken place in the historic center in recent years, including at Santo Domingo. Check current museum opening hours, room access and ticket arrangements for your chosen date rather than relying on older tourist descriptions.

## Frequently asked questions about Santo Domingo in Lima

### What is Santo Domingo Monastery known for?

Its arcades and historic courtyards, art collections and links with Peruvian Catholic saints. The complex is also associated with the early history of San Marcos University.

### Are Santo Domingo and Lima Cathedral the same building?

No. They are separate monuments in the historic center. [Lima Cathedral](/peru/place/lima-cathedral/) stands by Plaza Mayor, while Santo Domingo is a distinct Dominican monastery complex.

### Can I see the library and inner courtyards?

They belong to the complex's historic spaces, but actual access depends on the museum's operating rules and the condition of the rooms. Check which parts are open before visiting.

### Is the monastery in Lima connected with Coricancha?

No. The Santo Domingo church beside Coricancha is in Cusco. Santo Domingo Monastery in Lima has its own history connected with the Dominican order in the Peruvian capital.

### How much time should I allow for the monastery?

The scheduled stop on a city sightseeing tour is enough for an introductory visit. Allow additional time beyond that brief overview if you want to explore the art, courtyards and the order's history in detail.
